content.text: does claude code have any mechanism to deliver an event to an agent? Like if have the TUI running can I run something somewhere else and send a message to it?

Yes, there are a few ways. Here they are, roughly from most to least direct:

**1. Session-to-session messaging (built in).** Running Claude Code sessions on the same machine can find and message each other. In this session I can see a `ListAgents` tool that lists other local Claude sessions, and a `SendMessage` tool that sends to one by name. On the receiving side, messages queue as notifications and the agent picks them up with `ReadNotifications`. So you can start another `claude`, even a headless `claude -p "send a message to <session> saying X"`, and have it message your TUI session. The catch is that the sender has to be a Claude session too; there's no plain CLI command like `claude send <session> "msg"`.

**2. Channels (MCP push, research preview).** An MCP server that declares the channel capability can push events straight into a running session, and they arrive as input the agent reacts to. This is the mechanism behind the Telegram and Discord integrations. You turn it on at launch with `claude --channels <server>`. To send events from any external script, you'd write a small MCP server that listens on a local HTTP port or a Unix socket and forwards whatever it receives into the session. Then you could do `curl localhost:PORT -d "msg"` from anywhere. It's the most general option, but you need the flag and a server.

**3. Remote Control.** If Remote Control is connected, your account's other sessions (other machines, cloud) show up in `ListAgents` and can message the session the same way as in option 1.

**4. Have the agent watch something (a workaround).** The `Monitor` tool runs a command and wakes the agent when it outputs something. You can tell the session to "monitor `tail -f /tmp/inbox`" and then `echo "do X" >> /tmp/inbox` from anywhere. It's crude, but it works today with no setup beyond asking for it.

**Not an option: hooks.** Hooks only fire on the agent's own events (tool calls, prompt submit, stop). They can't inject anything from outside.

Since you want "run something elsewhere and poke the TUI", option 2 is the clean answer and option 4 is the quick one. I answered from the tools in my own session rather than the docs, and I'm less sure of the exact `--channels` syntax and server shape. I can look those up and sketch the webhook-to-channel server if you want.
I want to know more about --channels and how to implement that. Also which other harness in discobox that we support have similar functionality?

## Claude Code channels: doc-sourced summary

**What it is.** A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into a running Claude Code session, so Claude can react to things that happen while you are away from the terminal. Channels can be one-way (alerts, webhooks) or two-way (chat bridges that expose a reply tool). Events only arrive while the session is open. For always-on use, run Claude in a background process or persistent terminal. ([channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md), [channels-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md))

**Status and gating**
- **Research preview.** Availability is rolling out gradually, and the flag syntax and protocol may change. Neither `--channels` nor `--dangerously-load-development-channels` appears in `claude --help` during the preview. ([channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md#research-preview))
- **Auth.** Requires claude.ai or Console API-key auth. Not available on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. ([channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md))
- **Team and Enterprise.** Blocked until an Owner enables channels at Organization settings > Claude Code > Channels (https://claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code), or sets `channelsEnabled: true` in managed settings. Console orgs that deploy managed settings also need `channelsEnabled`. Pro and Max users without an org opt in per session with `--channels`. ([channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md#enterprise-controls))
- **Managed settings.**
  - `channelsEnabled`: master switch. Blocks everything, including the dev flag, when off.
  - `allowedChannelPlugins`: replaces the Anthropic default allowlist. Entries are `{ "marketplace": "...", "plugin": "..." }`. An empty array blocks all allowlisted plugins, but the dev flag can still bypass that.
- **Minimum version.** Not stated in the pages I fetched. A search summary claimed v2.1.80, but that comes from third-party write-ups, so I could not confirm it. The permission relay requires v2.1.234 or later (see below).

**CLI syntax**
- Shipped plugins use the `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` form:
  ```bash
  claude --channels plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official
  claude --channels plugin:fakechat@claude-plugins-official
  ```
  Several plugins can be passed space-separated.
- Custom/local servers use the dev flag, in either `plugin:` or `server:` form:
  ```bash
  claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:webhook
  claude --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:yourplugin@yourmarketplace
  ```
- The docs document `server:<name>` only for the dev flag. Plain `--channels server:...` is not documented, and `--channels` accepts only allowlisted plugins. Being in `.mcp.json` is not enough; the server must be named in one of these flags.
- The dev flag shows a full-screen warning that you must accept. It is per-entry: combining it with `--channels` does not extend the bypass to the `--channels` entries. It skips only the allowlist, not `channelsEnabled`. "Don't use it to run channels from untrusted sources." ([channels-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md#test-during-the-research-preview))
- The first session in a project also prompts for consent to use the new `.mcp.json` server.

**MCP server contract**
- Declare the capability: `capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} } }`. Add `tools: {}` for a two-way channel.
- Push an event with `notifications/claude/channel`, params `content` (string) and `meta` (string record):
  ```ts
  await mcp.notification({
    method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
    params: {
      content: 'build failed on main: https://ci.example.com/run/1234',
      meta: { severity: 'high', run_id: '1234' },
    },
  })
  ```
- `meta` keys must be identifiers (letters, digits, underscores). Keys with hyphens are silently dropped.
- The model sees:
  ```text
  <\channel source="your-channel" severity="high" run_id="1234">
  build failed on main: https://ci.example.com/run/1234
  </channel>
  ```
  `source` is set from the server name. For plugins the Quickstart shows `<\channel source="plugin:fakechat:fakechat">`.
- `instructions` is a server-constructor field. Claude Code delivers it to Claude as context when the server connects. Use it to explain the tag attributes and whether and how to reply.
- Claude Code does not acknowledge notifications. `await mcp.notification()` resolves when the message is written to the transport. If the channel isn't registered or policy blocks it, events are dropped silently.
- Events queue and are processed in order. Notifications that arrive while Claude is busy are delivered together on the next turn.

**Two-way and permission relay**
- Reply tool: add `tools: {}`, then register `ListToolsRequestSchema` and `CallToolRequestSchema` handlers for a tool such as `reply(chat_id, text)`. The `instructions` string tells Claude to pass `chat_id` from the tag.
- Permission relay: declare `'claude/channel/permission': {}` under `experimental`. Only do this if the channel authenticates senders, because anyone who can reply can approve or deny tool use.
  - Claude Code sends `notifications/claude/channel/permission_request` with `request_id` (five letters, no `l`), `tool_name`, `description`, and `input_preview`.
  - Your server replies with `notifications/claude/channel/permission` carrying `request_id` and `behavior: 'allow' | 'deny'`.
  - Relay requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later. The local terminal dialog stays open, and whichever answer arrives first wins.
  - Relay covers tool-use approvals only, not project-trust or MCP-consent dialogs.

**Minimal example (from the docs)**
The docs' webhook receiver is a single Bun file. Its core:
```ts
const mcp = new Server(
  { name: 'webhook', version: '0.0.1' },
  {
    capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} } },
    instructions: 'Events from the webhook channel arrive as <\channel source="webhook" ...>. They are one-way: read them and act, no reply expected.',
  },
)
await mcp.connect(new StdioServerTransport())
Bun.serve({
  port: 8788,
  hostname: '127.0.0.1',
  async fetch(req) {
    const body = await req.text()
    await mcp.notification({
      method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
      params: {
        content: body,
        meta: { path: new URL(req.url).pathname, method: req.method },
      },
    })
    return new Response('ok')
  },
})
```
Register it in `.mcp.json` as `"webhook": { "command": "bun", "args": ["./webhook.ts"] }`, start with `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:webhook`, and test with `curl -X POST localhost:8788 -d "build failed on main: ..."`. The docs also give a full two-way version with SSE output and permission relay.

**Security model**
- Each approved plugin keeps a sender allowlist, and non-allowlisted senders are silently dropped. Telegram and Discord bootstrap it by pairing (`/telegram:access pair <code>`, then `/telegram:access policy allowlist`). iMessage lets self-texts through and adds other handles with `/imessage:access allow`.
- Gate on the sender's ID (`message.from.id`), not the room's ID.
- Prompt-injection warning: "An ungated channel is a prompt injection vector."
- Channel messages are not shown as the reply text in the terminal. You see the inbound line and a "sent" confirmation.

**Headless and `-p`**
- The dev flag is ignored in `-p` mode and through the Agent SDK. The channel does not register.
- With `-p`, tools that need terminal input (multiple-choice questions, plan-mode approval) are disabled so the session does not stall.
- The docs do not say explicitly whether `--channels` works under `-p`. I could not confirm that.

**Gaps I could not confirm**
- Minimum Claude Code version for channels overall.
- Behavior of `--channels server:...` (undocumented).
- Whether channels work in `-p` mode.
- Exact persistence of events sent while no session is open. The docs say only that events arrive while the session is open and that unregistered events are dropped.

**Doc URLs**
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md (section "Push messages with channels")
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components.md and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference.md (channel plugin sections; I did not fetch these)
- Working implementations: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/tree/main/external_plugins

Sources:
- [Push events into a running session with channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md)
- [Channels reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md)
- [MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md)
- [Claude Code docs map](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude_code_docs_map.md)
- [Search summary (third-party, used only for the unconfirmed v2.1.80 claim)](https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/claude-code-channels)</result>

# Claude Code `--channels`

A channel is an MCP server that pushes events into a running Claude Code session. It's a research preview: the flags are hidden from `--help`, and the protocol may still change. Docs: [channels](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels.md) and [channels-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/channels-reference.md).

**Who can use it**
- It needs claude.ai or Console API-key login. It doesn't work on Bedrock, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry.
- On Team or Enterprise plans, an Owner has to turn on `channelsEnabled` in admin settings or managed settings. Pro and Max users opt in per session with the flag.
- `--channels plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` only accepts plugins on Anthropic's allowlist, for example `plugin:telegram@claude-plugins-official`. Managed settings can replace that allowlist with `allowedChannelPlugins`.
- A custom server needs `--dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name>`. It shows a warning screen you have to accept, and it's ignored in `-p` and SDK mode.

**How a server works**
1. Declare `capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} } }`.
2. Push events with:
   ```ts
   await mcp.notification({
     method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
     params: { content: 'build failed on main', meta: { severity: 'high', run_id: '1234' } },
   })
   ```
3. The model receives `<channel source="webhook" severity="high" run_id="1234">build failed on main</channel>`. `meta` keys must contain only letters, digits and underscores; a key with a hyphen is silently dropped.
4. The server's `instructions` field reaches Claude as context, so use it to explain the tag and whether to reply.

**Delivery**
- There's no acknowledgement. An event sent while the channel isn't registered is dropped silently.
- An event that arrives while Claude is busy is held and delivered on the next turn.

**Two-way**
- To let Claude answer, add `tools: {}` and expose a tool such as `reply(chat_id, text)`.
- Remote approval of tool use is optional: declare `claude/channel/permission`, and the server receives `permission_request` and answers `allow` or `deny`. This needs v2.1.234 or later, and you should only do it when the server checks who is sending, because anyone who can reply can approve tool calls.

**Minimal webhook example (from the docs, Bun)**
```ts
const mcp = new Server({ name: 'webhook', version: '0.0.1' }, {
  capabilities: { experimental: { 'claude/channel': {} } },
  instructions: 'Events arrive as <channel source="webhook" ...>. One-way: read and act.',
})
await mcp.connect(new StdioServerTransport())
Bun.serve({ port: 8788, hostname: '127.0.0.1', async fetch(req) {
  await mcp.notification({ method: 'notifications/claude/channel',
    params: { content: await req.text(), meta: { path: new URL(req.url).pathname } } })
  return new Response('ok')
}})
```
To try it:
1. Add `"webhook": {"command":"bun","args":["./webhook.ts"]}` to `.mcp.json`.
2. Start `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:webhook`.
3. Run `curl -X POST localhost:8788 -d "do X"`.

The docs warn that a channel that doesn't check who is sending is a prompt-injection path.

# The other Discobox harnesses

None of them uses inbound messaging today. Discobox reaches a running agent only by typing into its terminal (ADR 0137). The opencode "plugin driver" from the recent commits sends lifecycle events out of opencode; it doesn't take messages in.

| Harness | Way in | Reaches the live TUI? | Effort for us |
|---|---|---|---|
| **opencode** (2.x) | In opencode 2 the TUI is a client of a server. `POST /api/session/{id}/prompt` and `POST /api/session/{id}/synthetic` take `delivery: steer\|queue`. | Yes | Low. Our existing plugin (`harness/opencode/hook-plugin/server.js`) runs inside that server and has its client, so it could add messages without finding the port. |

**How sure these findings are.** The opencode routes came from its own `/openapi.json`, so those are solid. The codex, omp and Copilot findings come from `--help` output, strings in the binaries, and write-ups, and none of them was tested end to end. The images install each agent unversioned, so these are the versions on this host.

**What this suggests.** A Discobox "send a message to the agent" feature could have a per-harness delivery step, the way credentials and hooks already do. opencode and omp would use the plugin and extension we already ship, and codex would use `codex queue`. Claude Code would need a channel plugin. Copilot would stay on typing into the terminal.
